conceptual assets.information: The authentication-valid state is the one-bit authorization value loaded from wdata_i(0) or cleared when disabled; debug authentication depends on retaining this state, and valid_o reports it.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The authentication-valid state may be sensitive authentication status, and line 66 exposes authenticated_q directly on valid_o. An attacker able to alter the write path can forge or clear the state because wdata_i(0) loads it at line 57 and enable_i or we_i controls that update at lines 54-57. Holding enable_i low repeatedly clears the state at lines 54-55, so valid_o at line 66 cannot remain asserted and authenticated debug operation can be withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe valid_o and manipulate we_i, wdata_i, or enable_i to learn, forge, or clear the authentication state.

conceptual assets.information: The authentication-enable decision is enable_i's control of whether the authentication state is cleared or may be written; the authenticator's ability to retain an authenticated condition depends on it.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing enable_i changes authenticated_q through the clear assignment at lines 54-55, allowing unauthorized modification of authentication behavior. Holding enable_i low clears authenticated_q at lines 54-55 and withholds the asserted valid_o state at line 66, disabling authenticated operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force enable_i low to invalidate authentication or toggle it during a write to alter the resulting authorization state.

conceptual assets.information: The write-access command represented by we_i determines whether wdata_i can update the authentication state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing we_i at line 56 controls whether wdata_i(0) is committed to authenticated_q at line 57, permitting unauthorized authentication changes. Suppressing we_i prevents the required authentication write from reaching authenticated_q, so valid_o cannot be established or updated.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could assert we_i with a selected wdata_i value to forge authentication or suppress we_i to prevent authentication.

considered, not kept.reason: re_i is never read after its declaration at line 26, so it cannot cause an access or affect any information.
rdata_o is tied to zero at line 69, so it carries no changing state or secret and has no security-relevant mechanism.
busy_o is tied to zero at line 63 and does not report or control any operation.
clk_i only times the authenticated_q assignment at line 53 and is excluded as a conceptual asset by the clocks and resets rule.
rstn_i only resets authenticated_q at lines 51-52 and is excluded as a conceptual asset by the clocks and resets rule.
